note: End-to-end paths. Steps cost eight seconds each on the runner's clock, and waits are whole seconds, so the runner cannot express a gap shorter than eight seconds. The runner does not implement also_satisfies. Where a route depends on a hidden target (early_insulin, insulin_restart), the scenario names the target as a step straight after the order that earns it in the engine, and its note says so. DKA-tests.js folds the real routes through the engine with fractional times and is the authority.

scenarios.name: Intended path: glucose, gas and chemistry, fluid, potassium, a repeat level, insulin, the dextrose plan, handoff
Doing nothing: she stays as she arrived
scenarios.note: No clock changes her.

scenarios.name: Fluid alone changes no phase
scenarios.note: Covered through the crystalloid group.

scenarios.name: Potassium first reaches potassium_replaced
Potassium needs a line
scenarios.note: Blocked by the case prerequisite, which is the catalog's three-flag line rule.

scenarios.name: Potassium then an infusion reaches treated
Subcutaneous insulin after potassium also reaches treated
A bolus alone after potassium does not treat her
Insulin infusion first drives the potassium down
Subcutaneous insulin first does the same, with no line
An insulin bolus first does the same
Insulin a few seconds after potassium is still too early
scenarios.note: Insulin acts at ten seconds and the potassium needs twenty.

scenarios.name: Potassium alone does not rescue her while insulin runs
Holding insulin alone, with no potassium ever given, does not rescue her
Holding insulin and giving potassium rescues her
After the rescue, restarting insulin reaches treated
scenarios.note: One order in the recovering phase is the restart. insulin_restart is the hidden target that order earns in the engine.

scenarios.name: After the rescue she waits for the restart
scenarios.note: No order in the recovering phase, so no restart.

scenarios.name: Oral potassium does not count
scenarios.note: It has no effect at any point in the case.

scenarios.name: Bicarbonate changes no phase
scenarios.note: It shows on a repeat chemistry.

scenarios.name: Handoff from the potassium_falling phase completes the case
Glargine alone changes no phase
Glargine after insulin is running leaves her treated
Insulin twelve seconds after potassium still drives the potassium down
scenarios.note: This was the known gap of v0.23, closed on 7 October 2026. The potassium finishes first, and the early rule in potassium_replaced fires five seconds later. early_insulin is the hidden target the insulin order earns in the engine, because it was placed in the arrival phase.

scenarios.name: Insulin well after the potassium has finished reaches treated
scenarios.note: The order is placed in potassium_replaced, so it earns no hidden target.

scenarios.name: Potassium given before early insulin counts: the hold alone rescues her
scenarios.note: Intended. An infusion that is already running is still running, so the hold is the step that was missing.

scenarios.name: Potassium given before early insulin, and insulin never held: she stays weak
Bolus first, rescue, one infusion reaches treated
scenarios.note: The fault of v0.23: this learner needed the infusion ordered twice. Both hidden targets are named as steps.

scenarios.name: Bolus first, rescue, a second bolus alone does not treat her
scenarios.note: A bolus earns no restart.

scenarios.name: Subcutaneous first, rescue, one subcutaneous dose reaches treated
Two insulin orders before the hold are not a restart
scenarios.note: The gap of v0.23, closed on 7 October 2026: these two orders used to set the restart flag before the hold.

scenarios.name: Known gap: insulin reordered during the rescue wait is ignored
scenarios.note: She recovers although insulin was reordered, and the reorder is not the restart. Recorded so a fix shows up as a failing scenario.

scenarios.name: Known gap: a hold pressed before any insulin still counts as the hold
scenarios.note: Recorded so a fix shows up as a failing scenario.

scenarios.name: An insulin infusion with no line is blocked
scenarios.note: Blocked by the catalog's vascular access rule. Nothing is given, so nothing happens.

scenarios.name: Fluid by infusion alone, then the intended order, reaches treated
scenarios.note: A crystalloid infusion counts as her fluid. DKA-tests.js checks the credit and the monitor.

scenarios.name: Potassium through a central line needs no peripheral line
scenarios.note: The prerequisite is the catalog's three-flag rule.

scenarios.name: Two chemistries before the potassium change no phase
scenarios.note: The follow-up side of this is in DKA-tests.js. The runner does not model follow-ups.
